semanticFindings.assessment: The actual closed SemanticProof enum has Reflexivity, Decide, LinearArithmetic, Simplify, Constructor, Cases, Induction, Congruence, BooleanReflection and Apply. No direct transitivity/Have/Rewrite variant exists in this semantic grammar. This fact is not a proof of semantic composition impossibility.

Apply resolves exactly one existing semantic proof_rules member with explicit argument arity/types, then emits exact theorem arguments. Merely naming Prelude Eq.trans/congrArg does not register it as a semantic theorem. No implicit two-proof composition interface is established.

Simplify explicitly accepts theorem proof_rules and local Prop hypotheses as well as definitions/selected builtin bridges. Refs must be nonempty, strictly sorted and unique; emission is simp only [refs]. Thus theorem-rewriting is grammar-supported. An exact permitted empty-axiom construction and its cost are unproved. Existing no-Simplify scope is not waived; this review neither authorizes that tactic nor asserts the hypothetical exact proof necessarily introduces propext.

Cases/Induction require a named local whose type is Nat/List/document inductive; Prop and builtin Result do not satisfy that elimination path. Congruence emits congr1 without explicit proof-premise field. Existing Nat-family transport can carry a base equality but does not automatically prove the proposed two-certificate composition.
